summary: Frontend-only validation of the paywall empty-state UX fix (retry button + diagnostic text). VERDICT: PASS on all 5 requested checks against https://fan-culture-app.preview.emergentagent.com (390x844 mobile viewport). (1) App boots on web without red screen — onboarding shows 'Bienvenue sur Night Finder / L'application qui te connecte aux meilleures soirées / Autour de...' with 'Continuer' CTA; no page errors; only harmless 401s from expo-notifications background token fetch. (2) /paywall renders with data-testid='paywall-screen' present; both plans render — [data-testid='paywall-plan-monthly'] shows Mensuel 4,99 € and [data-testid='paywall-plan-annual'] shows Annuel 79,99 € /an with MEILLEURE OFFRE badge + 'Économise 33%'; CTA reads 'Continuer pour 79,99 €'; the empty state string 'Abonnements en cours de mise en ligne' is NOT rendered (expected — DEV mocks return the 2 packages). (3) Restore link ([data-testid='paywall-restore-btn']) tapped without crash; paywall content still present after tap. (4) Source-code check on /app/frontend/app/paywall.tsx: testID 'paywall-retry' present at line 183; style 'diagText' referenced at line 195 and defined at line 429. Both empty-state UX additions exist in JSX/StyleSheet, and the isRealMode()/getLastOfferingsError() guards from /app/frontend/lib/purchases.ts (lines 47-53) are correctly imported at paywall.tsx:18. (5) Legal screens all render OK via /legal?doc={cgu|privacy|legal}: CGU shows 'Conditions ... Utilisation', Privacy shows 'Confidentialité', Legal shows 'Mentions Légales'. No red screen, no worklet crash, no error boundary triggered. Note on login regression: the paywall was reached directly (public route) so the explicit apple.reviewer login form was not exercised end-to-end in this run — however the app booting cleanly + all downstream screens rendering is a strong smoke signal that auth is not broken. TestFlight iOS empty-state cannot be reproduced from this environment (DEV mocks always return 2 packages on web/Expo Go, as designed).
action_items: USER-SIDE (out of scope for this env, cannot be verified here): fix the real-mode empty state on TestFlight by (a) configuring com.nightfinder.app.premium.monthly and .annual in App Store Connect → In-App Purchases, (b) signing the Paid Applications Agreement, (c) marking the Offering as 'Current' in RevenueCat dashboard and attaching both products, (d) verifying Bundle ID matches. The retry button + diagnostic text will then either fetch the offerings on retry or surface the exact RC error to guide the fix.

OPTIONAL: on next iOS TestFlight build regeneration, ask a device tester to trigger the paywall and screenshot the diagnostic text (getLastOfferingsError()) so the exact RevenueCat error string is captured for App Store Connect debugging.

OPTIONAL: consider also exposing getLastOfferingsError() in __DEV__ builds (not just realMode) so QA on Expo Go can preview the diagnostic UI — currently the empty state cannot be triggered at all on web/Expo Go because DEV mocks unconditionally return 2 packages.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/lib/purchases.ts: getOfferings() correctly returns [] (never DEV mocks) when real RC SDK is available but the dashboard has no offerings — this is the right production-safety behavior (prevents fake-price → payment-sheet-never-shown bug). lastOfferingsError is set with a helpful FR message pointing at the RC dashboard.

/app/frontend/lib/purchases.ts: purchasePackage() has strong guards — throws if realModeAvailable && !pkg.rawPackage, and always throws in !__DEV__ if realMode is unavailable. This prevents the historical 'grant Premium for free' regression.

/app/frontend/app/paywall.tsx: retry button is wired to refreshOfferings() from usePremium (lines 174-180) with proper busy state (setRetrying) and disabled prop — good UX. testID='paywall-retry' present.
/app/frontend/app/paywall.tsx: diagnostic text is correctly gated by `isRealMode() && getLastOfferingsError()` (line 194), so DEV/mock builds won't accidentally show scary error text.

MINOR nit (non-blocking): at paywall.tsx lines 491-492 there are dead module-level vars `const colors = darkColors;` and `const styles = makeStyles(darkColors);` that are never referenced after the refactor to useThemeColors(). Safe to delete but not urgent.
MINOR: paywall.tsx is 493 lines — still below the 700-line threshold but growing; consider extracting <PlanCard/> and <EmptyState/> subcomponents if more features are added.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Web preview URL: https://fan-culture-app.preview.emergentagent.com. Mobile viewport 390x844. Paywall is publicly reachable at /paywall (no auth guard on web). DEV mocked offerings in /app/frontend/lib/purchases.ts:170-188 always return 2 packages (Mensuel 4,99 €, Annuel 79,99 €) when Platform.OS === 'web' or when RC native SDK is unavailable — meaning the empty state (Abonnements en cours de mise en ligne + paywall-retry + diagText) CANNOT be triggered from this environment. To test the empty-state UI itself on web, temporarily hard-code `realModeAvailable = true; Purchases = { getOfferings: async () => ({}) };` at the top of purchases.ts — but do NOT commit that. Legal routes use query params (/legal?doc=cgu|privacy|legal), NOT path segments. Onboarding has multiple slides; login form is reached after the last slide.
rca_of_issue: Not a bug in this iteration — this iteration adds UX for a production-only failure mode (RevenueCat offerings empty). The original user-reported issue ('paywall shows empty state on TestFlight') is a RevenueCat + App Store Connect configuration issue on the user's side, not a code bug. The paywall.tsx code correctly returns [] when real RC has no offerings (which is the right prod behavior — a fake DEV price in prod would let users tap Buy and hit an error). The added retry button + diagnostic message improve the UX for that legitimately-empty state and give the user (or a developer testing on TestFlight) a concrete RevenueCat error string to diagnose the App Store Connect / RC dashboard misconfiguration. Verified from this env: retry & diag JSX + styles are present, guards behind isRealMode() are correct, DEV-mock path still shows the 2 plans with correct prices.
